assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal W\), \(\mathcal A\), and every \(\mathcal X_t\) are specified finite alphabets, with \(|\mathcal A|\ge2\) and \(|\mathcal X_t|\ge2\).
The substantive law factorizes as \(p_W(w)p_A(a\mid w)K_1(x_1\mid w,a)\prod_{t=2}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})\).
Every entry of \(p_W\), \(p_A\), and \(K_t\) is strictly positive.
The exogenous disturbances of the substantive structural equations are mutually independent.

standard.name: Locally monotone response mechanism with local substantive parents

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((W,A,X)\), the continuation coins \(C_1,\ldots,C_T\) are mutually independent.
For every legal argument and every \(t\), \(0<q_t(w,a,x_{S_t})<1\).
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)\).

definitions.name: Positive local monotone-dropout audit class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}=\{P: P\text{ is indexed by }T,S,B,e\text{ and satisfies }\text{ass:finite-alphabets},\text{ass:substantive-markov},\text{ass:substantive-positivity},\text{ass:markovian-scm},\text{ass:local-hazards},\text{ass:response-noise-independence},\text{ass:hazard-positivity},\text{ass:audit-randomization},\text{ass:audit-positivity}\}\). Allowed arrows may have null effects.

definitions.name: Dropout subdensities
definitions.construction: For \(d<T\), \(g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})=p_W(w)p_A(a\mid w)K_1(x_1\mid w,a)\prod_{t=2}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})\{\prod_{s=1}^{d}q_s(w,a,x_{S_s})\}\{1-q_{d+1}(w,a,x_{S_{d+1}})\}\); for \(d=T\), omit the final failure factor and retain \(\prod_{s=1}^{T}q_s(w,a,x_{S_s})\).

definitions.name: Audit-pattern tables
definitions.construction: Let \(I_d=\{1,\ldots,d\}\cup B_d\). Define \(M_d(w,a,x_{I_d})=\sum_{x_j:\,j\notin I_d}g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})\) for \(d<T\), and \(M_T=g_T\).

definitions.name: Graphwise identification of the entire endpoint vector
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\iff[\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P')\Rightarrow Q(P)=Q(P')]\) for every \(P,P'\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) using the same known \(e\).

definitions.name: Interval-block certificate handle
definitions.construction: Starting from \((M_d)_{d=0}^T\), maintain dropout-indexed interval boundary factors and transported endpoint linear functionals; close them under pattern marginalization and addition, local conditional-kernel normalization, Markov tail transport, positive-scaling duality, strict-concavity recovery, and exhaustive support-and-rank branching. A residual state must be converted into a graph-compatible positive response-fiber obstruction rather than passed to generic quantifier elimination.

definitions.name: Certificate criterion
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\iff\mathsf A(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)\) terminates with a recovery certificate for every positive support-and-rank branch.

definitions.name: Inclusion-minimal sufficient design frontier
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(T,S,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=\{B:\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1,\;\mathsf C(T,S,B',( |\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=0\text{ for every }B'\lneq B\}\), where \(B'\le B\) means \(B'_d\subseteq B_d\) for every \(d<T\).

statements.statement: For a fixed known \(e\), the law of \(O\) and the family \((M_d)_{d=0}^T\), together with the always-observed \((W,A)\) law, determine each other by finite linear transformations. In particular, for \(d<T\), each audited cell equals \(e_d(H_d)M_d\), and every unaudited cell is \((1-e_d(H_d))\) times the corresponding routine marginal.
statements.justification: This reduction isolates exactly what the randomized partial audit adds at the population level.
statements.gap: Levis et al. use the audit coin to recover a complete-data complement; here the identified primitive is only a dropout-specific marginal table.
statements.consumer: Every identification certificate and finite-table estimator starts from \((M_d)_{d=0}^T\), so the result separates design information from response-mechanism algebra.

statements.statement: For each \(d<T\), there is a positive function \(u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})\), with \(b_d=\min\{T,d+2\}\), such that \(g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})=u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})\prod_{t=b_d+1}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})\). Consequently, for \(b_d\le k<\ell\le T\), \(P(X_\ell\mid X_k,W,A,D=d)=K_{k+1}\cdots K_\ell\).
statements.justification: The factorization turns nonconsecutive audit measurements into legal composed transition kernels and bounds every local elimination state by an interval frontier.
statements.gap: The passive monotone results normalize response kernels; they do not exploit a substantive Markov suffix observed through partial audits.
statements.consumer: The interval-block calculus uses this lemma to transport an identified boundary marginal to the endpoint without recovering the missing trajectory.

statements.statement: Construct the finite procedure \(\mathsf A(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)\) from the interval-block certificate handle and prove the following exhaustive alternative on every positive support-and-rank branch. Either it returns an evaluable map \(\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}\) satisfying \(\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}((M_d)_{d=0}^T)=Q(P)\) for every compatible \(P\), or it returns two laws \((P,P')=\mathsf{Wit}_{T,S,B}\) in \(\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) such that \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P')\) and \(Q(P)\ne Q(P')\). The obstruction compiler must preserve strict positivity, the first-order substantive Markov factorization, every local parent set \(S_t\), and every audit table \(M_d\), and the proof must hold for arbitrary \(T\) and the specified alphabet sizes.
statements.justification: This is the answer-open mathematical kernel: it must unify rational normalization, rank-free curvature recovery, alphabet-sensitive branches, endpoint-only cancellations, and positive countermodel gluing.
statements.gap: Tikka and Karvanen provide separate sufficient recoveries and one passive obstruction; no published result gives a complete partial-audit recovery-or-obstruction alternative for a restricted substantive Markov chain.
statements.consumer: A longitudinal study designer can certify whether historical chart or survey variables in each dropout stratum suffice for the endpoint treatment contrast before fielding the audit.

statements.statement: The certificate criterion is necessary and sufficient: \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\). On the affirmative side, \(\mathsf A\) returns \(\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}\); on the negative side, it returns \(\mathsf{Wit}_{T,S,B}\). This equivalence holds simultaneously for every endpoint coordinate \(Q_a(x)\) and every positive law, including null allowed-arrow effects and deficient observable-kernel ranks.
statements.justification: An iff theorem distinguishes a design rule from another sufficient recovery recipe and makes failure operational through a legal countermodel.
statements.gap: Theorems 1--6 of Tikka and Karvanen neither use partial audit margins nor characterize intervention-target identification; Levis et al. require full phase-two recovery.
statements.consumer: The theorem decides whether a planned partial recontact protocol supports the five-year treatment-specific weight distribution in an EHR cohort under the declared local dropout graph.

statements.statement: Testing \(\mathsf C\) on all \(2^{T(T+1)/2}\) bundle designs and deleting every success that strictly contains another success returns exactly \(\mathfrak F(T,S,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)\). Moreover, sufficiency is monotone: if \(B\le B'\) and \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\), then \(\mathsf C(T,S,B',( |\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\).
statements.justification: The focal design object is the complete antichain of minimal sufficient measurement bundles, not a single sufficient protocol.
statements.gap: Existing monotone-MNAR and double-sampling results fix the observed or recovered record and do not enumerate minimal partial-recovery designs.
statements.consumer: Investigators can compare only irreducible protocols when assigning the costs of chart abstraction, laboratory assays, or tracing interviews.

statements.statement: As a required reduction, suppose exactly one hazard may depend on a substantive state: \(S_k=\{j\}\), where \(j\in\{k,k+1\}\), and \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\). Then \(\mathsf C=1\) if and only if there are \(d<k\) and \(\ell\ge j\) with \(\ell\in B_d\). The minimal frontier consists exactly of the singleton designs \(B_d=\{\ell\}\) with all other bundles empty and \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).
statements.justification: This arbitrary-horizon reduction forces the general calculus to reproduce a tractable boundary and its positive gamma-swap obstruction.
statements.gap: The anchor proves passive nonidentification along a self-censoring path but does not state when a downstream audit destroys the cancellation or enumerate minimal audits.
statements.consumer: It gives a closed-form measurement rule when scientific knowledge isolates one informative dropout hazard.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathsf C=1\) and the returned reconstruction has a continuously differentiable local extension \(F\) at \(o\) with finite derivative. Then \(F(\widehat o_n)\to Q\) in probability and \(\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-Q\}\Rightarrow N(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top)\). The same result holds for inverse-probability audit tables after composing with their fixed known-\(e\) linear map.
statements.justification: Regular branches of the constructive reconstruction yield estimators and a joint limit law without pretending that rank-changing branches are smooth.
statements.gap: Levis et al. transform a full-data influence function after complete follow-up; the derivative here belongs to a partial-bundle reconstruction that may be implicit.
statements.consumer: A sufficient audited EHR design obtains standard errors for every treatment-specific endpoint probability on its regular identified strata.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge1\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), every design \(B\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\), the projected set \(\mathcal C_n\) satisfies \(\Pr_P\{Q(P)\in\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its coordinate extrema are finite constrained polynomial optimization problems after closure, because \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}\) is polynomial in the finite primitive tables with known \(e\).
statements.justification: Projection supplies honest finite-sample coverage on singular and nonidentified strata without upgrading generic optimization into the headline identification algorithm.
statements.gap: Existing smooth double-sampling intervals do not cover rank-changing or nonidentified partial-audit laws; Duarte et al. supply the adjacent polynomial-program representation rather than this design-specific cube projection.
statements.consumer: Studies whose chosen bundle is insufficient, or whose data lie near a singular branch, still obtain globally valid uncertainty sets for endpoint intervention probabilities.

sampling_model.design: Known randomized second-stage audit within each dropout stratum, with a fixed bundle \(B_d\) and probability \(e_d(H_d)\).
sampling_model.units: Independent records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from the positive finite SCM class.
sampling_model.treatment: Observational treatment \(A\) has a strictly positive conditional law given \(W\); intervention replaces that kernel by \(A=a\).
sampling_model.overlap: All substantive table entries and all legal continuation and audit probabilities are strictly positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Use empirical observed-cell frequencies or Horvitz--Thompson audit-pattern tables with known \(e_d\); apply the returned finite reconstruction on a compatible regular branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Monotonicity permits several response-kernel recoveries yet a mediated self-censoring path makes the corresponding marginal and target laws nonidentified.
A categorical colluder propensity is identified if and only if its observable colluder matrices have full column rank.
Randomized intensive follow-up identifies and efficiently estimates smooth complete-data functionals when the phase-two variables complete the coarsened record.
In ordinary nonmonotone missing-data DAGs, absence of self-censoring and colluder obstructions characterizes full-law identification.
A sound intervention tree yields constructive target-law identification but is not complete.
Finite discrete causal queries admit sharp bounds through polynomial programming and convergent branch-and-bound.

tldr: Randomized recontact can identify a longitudinal intervention endpoint without recovering either the full missing trajectory or the endpoint among every audited dropout, but no existing theorem decides which partial measurement bundles suffice. The project seeks a finite interval-block certificate calculus for positive finite Markov chains with locally informative monotone hazards. Its central alternative returns either an evaluable endpoint reconstruction from dropout-indexed audit tables or two strictly positive graph-compatible SCMs with the same observed law and different endpoint intervention distributions. The resulting iff criterion generates the complete antichain of inclusion-minimal audit designs; plug-in Gaussian inference is derived on regular branches, and observed-cell projection gives finite-sample coverage on singular or nonidentified branches.

project_justification.gap: Passive monotone-MNAR theory supplies local recovery operations and a self-censoring-path obstruction, while randomized double-sampling theory assumes that phase two completes the missing record. Neither decides endpoint identification when each dropout stratum reveals only a fixed subset of future coordinates.
project_justification.niche: The local-parent Markov-chain restriction is narrow enough to expose interval boundaries and transport kernels, yet rich enough to exhibit deficient-rank concavity recovery, alphabet-sensitive identification, overlapping-bundle failure, and endpoint-only cancellation.
project_justification.fill: A constructive recovery-or-positive-obstruction calculus yields the exact graph-and-pattern criterion, an evaluable reconstruction, and every inclusion-minimal sufficient bundle design for arbitrary horizon.

related_work: Tikka and Karvanen (2025) show that deterministic monotonicity can rescue colluder structures and can create nonidentification along mediated self-censoring paths; their Discussion explicitly leaves a complete monotone criterion open. Tikka and Karvanen (2024) derive categorical colluder equations whose full-column-rank condition is necessary and sufficient for their full-law propensity target, motivating but not resolving the present positive rank strata. Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) characterize full-law identification for ordinary nonmonotone missing-data DAGs through an odds-ratio construction that cannot be evaluated on forbidden monotone patterns. Guo and Nabi (2026) track selection-bias propagation through a constructive intervention tree, but state that the algorithm is sound rather than complete and does not incorporate restrictions on the substantive law. Levis et al. (2024) identify smooth complete-data functionals after randomized intensive follow-up when phase two recovers the entire missing complement; a fixed bundle in this project may leave both an endpoint and another hazard parent unmeasured. Duarte et al. (2024) provide a polynomial-program oracle for each fixed finite instance, which is used for bounded verification and projected confidence sets rather than as the graph-explicit arbitrary-horizon criterion. Karvanen and Tikka (2024) and Bhattacharya et al. (2019) establish that target-law recovery need not coincide with full-law recovery, supporting the endpoint-specific state carried by the proposed calculus.
technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing interval-block alternative and its positive obstruction-gluing theorem are open. The first rule system must recover the complementary-audit strict-concavity case and the binary bridge case, and it must reject the supplied four-visit overlapping-bundle counterexample. The exhaustive comparison over all \(1024\) designs for that fixed four-visit graph is an early kill test. A rule set that fails this audit must be abandoned or enlarged before an arbitrary-horizon induction. Generic real quantifier elimination, numerical fiber searches, and the finite polynomial confidence computation do not satisfy the identification theorem.
honest_scope: The proposal claims no completed arbitrary-horizon criterion. Exact audit-table equivalence, the local tail factorization, the single-hazard frontier, the complementary-audit concavity mechanism, the binary-versus-larger bridge boundary, and explicit positive counterexamples provide verified proof architecture that must be re-established in the paper. The open content is the exhaustive block state, every positive rank branch, endpoint-only cancellations, termination, and graph-compatible positive gluing. As sanity reductions, empty audit bundles must reproduce passive identification exactly when every local hazard uses only lagged states; auditing \(X_T\) in every dropout stratum must identify the endpoint by summing strata; and the certificate must reproduce the stated single-hazard proposition. No shadow-variable rank, parametric selection, missing-at-random, or faithfulness restriction is imposed. No polynomial-time guarantee is claimed.

literature_map.settled: Passive monotonicity licenses several legal-pattern propensity recoveries and creates positive self-censoring-path countermodels; nonmonotone full-law completeness and a sound intervention-tree procedure are available.
literature_map.unsettled: No opened source supplies a complete target-law criterion under deterministic monotone response logic, local Markov restrictions, and dropout-specific partial audits.
literature_map.occupation_check: The exact target is unoccupied in the opened theorem texts. Guo and Nabi explicitly state that their tree is incomplete and does not incorporate substantive-law restrictions.

literature_map.settled: A categorical colluder propensity is recovered by full-column-rank matrix equations, and arbitrary finite discrete causal fibers can be bounded by polynomial programming.
literature_map.unsettled: Deficient rank can still identify an endpoint through normalization or curvature, and no source classifies all positive partial-audit strata into recovery versus a target-varying fiber.
literature_map.occupation_check: The anchor concerns full-law colluders and treats rank deficiency as failure for its propensity target; it does not subsume target-specific partial-audit recovery.

literature_map.settled: Known randomized second-stage probabilities identify a complete-data distribution and yield efficient estimators when follow-up supplies the entire complement of the coarsened record.
literature_map.unsettled: A fixed bundle may omit the endpoint and other hazard parents, so complete-record conditioning and its influence-function transformation are unavailable.
literature_map.occupation_check: The general-coarsening proposition explicitly assumes that the phase-two complement and phase-one record jointly recover the complete datum.

literature_map.settled: Target-law identification can survive failure of full-law identification, and factorizable imputation is valid for certain orderings.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither source gives an arbitrary-horizon endpoint-specific state space that tracks cancellations across partially audited dropout strata.
literature_map.occupation_check: The exact audit-design frontier is not present; this thread supports retaining endpoint functions rather than requiring full trajectory recovery.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem is Tikka and Karvanen's 2025 passive monotone result: its Theorems 1--5 recover response kernels from legal all-one patterns, while Theorem 6 constructs a self-censoring-path gamma swap. The proposed theorem changes the information structure by adding randomized same-subject margins that can reveal only selected post-dropout coordinates. This creates recovery by positive scaling and strict concavity at deficient rank, alphabet-dependent endpoint recovery, and overlapping-bundle failures that are not implied by either half of the anchor. Levis et al. identify complete-data functionals only when intensive follow-up recovers the whole complement of the coarsened record. The new strict delta is an explicit finite graph-and-audit-pattern criterion that is necessary and sufficient for the intervention endpoint alone, together with an evaluable reconstruction on success, a legal positive Markovian countermodel compiler on failure, and the complete inclusion-minimal bundle frontier for arbitrary horizon. Generic polynomial decidability is retained only as a bounded oracle and cannot satisfy this delta.
